chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Do not go out (on a journey) during Ramadan, except for Hajj or Umrah, or for wealth that you fear might be lost, or for crops whose harvest time has arrived."

key_terms.رَمَضَانُ: The month of fasting in the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.لِلْحَجِّ: For the major pilgrimage to Mecca

ai.seo_question: What are the valid reasons for traveling during Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the general prohibition against traveling during Ramadan is lifted for specific necessities: performing Hajj or Umrah, securing perishable wealth, or harvesting crops. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential balance between spiritual devotion and practical livelihood, ensuring that essential economic and religious duties are not neglected during the holy month.
